paragraphs.notes: The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese. The page body is a single running alphabetical enumeration of herbicide common names that begins on the previous page and continues on the next; it is not a sentence and carries no paragraph number, as WO publications of this vintage do not number paragraphs. The list is almost entirely trade or common names, which are language-neutral and are carried across unchanged into en; only the German connective wording and the spelled-out chemical names are translated there, so the two fields differ only in those places. Punctuation is as printed, including the commas rather than semicolons in 'dimethazone, clomazon', 'dimetrasulfuron, dinitramine' and 'metabenzuron, methobenzuron'. Names are transcribed as printed and not corrected: 'flumeturon' is printed thus (the ISO common name is fluometuron), 'clomazon', 'isocarbamid' and 'mefluidid' keep their German endings, and 'F5231' is printed without a space while 'EL 77', 'MT 128', 'MT 5950' and 'NC 310' are printed with one. Line-end hyphens in '1H-pyrazole-4-/carboxamid', '5-[4-(3-/fluorpropyl)', '6-Chlor-N-/(3-chlor-2-propenyl)' and 'N-[3-Chlor-4-/(1-methylethyl)' belong to the chemical names and are joined without a space. A small stray ink mark sits just below the 'r' of 'cyprazole' on the third body line; it is a scan artifact, not a character.
